title: Northpine TeleCare — RLHF & Safety Gotchas (scratchbook)
content:
Call notes + working scratchbook for Northpine TeleCare (urgent safety + RLHF concerns). Written fast after sync w/ client SE + product lead (notes to self). Not polished — use for follow-ups and handoff to privacy/compliance.

Meeting context:
- Date: 2025-02-11, 11:00 PST (30m)
- Attendees: Northpine: Dr. Mira Solano (clinical lead), Arjun Patel (eng), Lucia Park (privacy ops). Redwood: Aisha (SE), Diego (applied ML).
- Ask: prototype a triage assistant that summarizes patient-reported symptoms and suggests next-step disposition (self-care, nurse follow-up, urgent escalation). Must run in customer VPC with strict PHI isolation; they want the option to keep model weights on-prem for highest-sensitivity clinics.

Key constraints they repeated:
- No PHI leaves their VPC. TeleCare will run inference inside their Azure VNet; control plane in Redwood hosted minimal only for licensing/pulse metrics (they are OK with telemetry as long as no PII/PHI is included).
- Audit trail required for every inference (prompt, model version, decision rationale) stored in their encrypted blob store.
- Latency target: median end-to-end < 600ms for summary path (text-only triage). Peak: 1500 reqs/min for regional clinic.
- Accuracy requirement: false-negative escalation rate must be < 1.2% on a defined eval set (client will provide historical triage transcripts).

Immediate RLHF + safety gotchas we flagged during call (capture for AE/Product/Security):
1) Hallucinated medication instructions: models tend to invent doses if asked to summarize or synthesize care plans. For triage, that is catastrophic. Must ensure generation policy forbids giving dosing/administration instructions — instead the assistant should say "refer to clinician" or supply vetted, static guidance from their canonical content store.
2) Implicit clinical inference: model may infer diagnosis language from ambiguous symptoms ("sounds like flu" vs "possible viral syndrome"). Client wants conservative language; need a calibrated conservative classifier or a post-processing filter to downgrade assertive statements.
3) PHI tokenization leaks: prompts that include free-text patient identifiers (addresses, MRNs) get cached in model KV unless we control cache policy. For private deployment, ensure KV cache masking and that cached KV is zeroed for PHI fields. Evaluate Redwood runtime's prefix caching knobs for VPC/on-prem.
4) Auditability vs privacy: audit requirement asks to log prompt + model output, but storing prompts with PHI in logs is disallowed externally. Must design a local hashing/PII-redaction layer: store a redacted copy externally and full logs locally in customer's encrypted store.
5) Tooling & function calls: client wants structured output (JSON disposition + confidence score). Must avoid over-reliance on free-text; prefer function/tool-calling style (explicit schema) so outputs can be validated before writing to EMR.
6) Behavioral drift after quantization: Northpine expressed interest in q4-bit to reduce cost. We need to run evals: quantized variants may change calibration; tie regressions to their eval set and gating rules.
7) Prompt injection from patient transcripts: patients may paste web text with instructions or URLs; model could follow unsafe instructions. Need input sanitization and a "dangerous content" classifier pre-check.
8) Emergency triggers: if model output suggests imminent harm, auto-escalate to human clinician but also avoid false-positives — define clear thresholds and human-in-the-loop flow.

Technical notes / potential implementation patterns to propose:
- Private Deploy (VPC) + Local Audit: deploy Redwood Private with a small control plane agent inside their VNet. Route all inference to on-prem (customer-managed GPUs) for highest-sensitivity clinics. For clinics that can tolerate hosted, use dedicated pools with VPC peering.
- Redaction pipeline: lightweight preprocessor that redacts PHI tokens (MRN, SSN, phone, DOB) before sending to any external service. Keep the full plaintext only in their encrypted blob store. Implement deterministic hashing for linking records across logs without exposing raw values.
- Structured outputs via function-calling: provide a JSON schema (disposition, urgency_code [0/1/2], rationale_snippet, confidence) and post-validate. If schema validation fails, escalate to human review.
- Conservative language model wrapper: add a calibration layer that maps model logits to conservative thresholds; also post-process assertions to add hedging language. Alternatively pipe model outputs through a secondary classifier trained on client-provided transcripts to flag assertive claims.
- Safety evaluation harness: Redwood Optimize eval job: run 3 variants (full-precision, 8-bit, 4-bit) on their labelled historical set; compare FN escalation rate, hallucination rate (medication/dose hallucinations), and calibration. Gate deploys by regression delta > 0.2% in FN.
- Tokenization & KV control: ensure KV cache is disabled for any request that contains PHI tokens, or run in single-request mode for those calls. Document runtime config options and provide a safe default.

Open questions (need answers from Northpine or internal teams):
- Which exact fields in transcripts are considered PHI by their legal team? (they mentioned MRN and SSN but clinicians often include family history that may be sensitive). Need a checklist from Lucia.
- Can they accept anonymized telemetry (token counts + timing) to Redwood control plane? They said yes in-principle but want examples of what telemetry looks like.
- Do they want model weights to be physically on their machines for all clinics or only "sensitive" clinics? Implications for cost/latency and rollout complexity.
- What is the required retention period for audit logs? (30/90/365 days affects storage & encryption rotate policies).
- Are there existing canonical guidance documents (approved care text) to use as a static response repository? If so, we can implement retrieval-augmented-reply and avoid free-form generated care instructions.

Concrete next steps (owner tags inline):
- Aisha: draft high-level proposal (1-pager) laying out two deployment options: fully on-prem vs hybrid (hosted for low-sensitivity). Include cost/latency tradeoffs and RLHF risk table. Due: 2025-02-18.
- Diego: spin up quick Optimize eval job skeleton for their sample set (they agreed to share 1500 triage transcripts). Use model variants: cgpt-3.8-med (fp16), cgpt-3.8-med-q8, cgpt-3.8-med-q4. Baseline metrics: FN rate, hallucination count (med doses), calibration (Brier). Due: 2025-02-21.
- Priya: coordinate with Lucia (privacy) to draft redaction checklist (which fields to redact/hash) and acceptable telemetry schema. Due: 2025-02-17.
- Aisha + Product: scope a safe defaults runtime config doc: KV cache rules, function-calling schema, emergency escalation thresholds. Put draft on Confluence and share with Northpine. Due: 2025-02-24.
- Sales/AE: confirm procurement timeline and willingness to sign on with a 6-month pilot vs PoC (they prefer pilot with limited on-prem hours).

Risks and mitigation (short):
- Risk: Model outputs giving unauthorized clinical instructions. Mitigation: RAR (retrieval-augmented response) from canonical guidance + canonical "do not give dosing" fallback text; block free-text clinical instruction completions.
- Risk: PHI logged to hosted telemetry. Mitigation: redaction + local-only full logs + external hashed linking.
- Risk: Regression after quantization. Mitigation: automatic eval gate + rollback policy + canary on 5% traffic.

Notes to self (implementation details we should remember):
- Add a runtime flag: redact_and_hash=true that clients can toggle per-route. Store hashed identifiers using HMAC with customer-provided key (not Redwood key).
- Provide a prebuilt function-calling JSON schema template for triage -> disposition -> urgency -> rationale snippet. Ship with a lightweight validator in SDKs (JS/Python).
- For emergency triggers, prefer a separate synchronous path that summons clinician UI; don't rely on async batch outputs for immediate escalation.

Draft client messaging points (short):
- "We can run inside your VNet with a local audit trail and configurable privacy filters; our platform supports function-style structured output to avoid free-form clinical instructions, and we will gate any reduced-precision model variants against your historical triage set before they see production traffic."

Immediate calendar asks:
- Request: sample dataset (anonymized) + explicit PHI field list by 2025-02-14.
- Follow-up: 1-hr architecture deep-dive with engineering (Arjun + Diego + Aisha) week of 2025-02-17.

Random scratch tidbits (brain dump):
- Might be worth proposing a "trusted templates" feature: admin-managed canned replies for common dispositions (pre-approved by clinicians) that the model can only select/annotate rather than generate. Reduces risk.
- Could run a short sim: fuzz patient text with injected dosing prompts to measure hallucination propensity. Use as demo for compliance.

End of scratchbook. Convert into a cleaner scope doc once we get dataset + PHI checklist.

-- Aisha K. (post-call quick capture)
